parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text: Use the answer to (a)(i) to show that the SI base units of pressure are kg m^{-1} s^{-2}.
parts.question_text_latex: Use the answer to (a)(i) to show that the SI base units of pressure are kg $m^{-1}$ $s^{-2}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A horizontal pipe has length L and a circular cross‑section of radius R. A liquid of density ρ
flows through the pipe. The mass m of liquid flowing through the pipe in time t is given by
m =(π (p_{2}- p_{1})R^{4}ρ t)/(8kL)
where p_{1} and p_{2} are the pressures at the ends of the pipe and k is a constant.
Determine the SI base units of k.
SI base units
parts.question_text_latex:
A horizontal pipe has length L and a circular cross‑section of radius R. A liquid of density $\rho$
flows through the pipe. The mass m of liquid flowing through the pipe in time t is given by
$m =\frac{\pi (p_{2}- p_{1})R^{4}\rho t}{8kL}$
where $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$ are the pressures at the ends of the pipe and k is a constant.
Determine the SI base units of k.
SI base units

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
An experiment is performed to determine the value of k by measuring the values of the other
quantities in the equation in (b).
The values of L and R each have a percentage uncertainty of 2%.
State and explain, quantitatively, which of these two quantities contributes more to the
percentage uncertainty in the calculated value of k.
